records.label: First brother
quotes: Two brothers are described with a severe syndrome of postnatal growth and mental retardation which includes extreme microcephaly, obesity developing during infancy, microgonadismsm, and a characteristic amphora-shaped facies.
The neurological exam is highly abnormal, with hypertonia and hyperreflexia, nystagmus, and an extremely irritable and agitated behavior.
The first child, who died at 4/1/2 years, also presented neonatal hypoglycemia and chronic constipation.

The neurological exam is highly abnormal, with hypertonia and hyperreflexia, nystagmus, and an extremely irritable and agitated behavior.

records.label: Large three-generation family
records.segregation: Disease locus linked to Xp21.1-p22.13, flanked by CYBB and DXS365
quotes: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity. Life expectancy of patients is less than two years.
Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, to a region that is flanked by CYBB and DXS365.

phenotypes.text: abnormal enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae and electron dense bodies

quotes: We describe a child with MEHMO and lactic acidosis whose muscle biopsy revealed markedly reduced activities of complexes 1,3 and 4 of the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
Histological staining showed mitochondrial proliferation and lipid storage. Electron microscopy revealed abnormal and enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae and electron dense bodies.

records.label: III:1
records.segregation: cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family; female carriers
quotes: Additionally, each of the affected individuals had unique symptoms including cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairments (individual III:1), generalized seizures (III:2), and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity (II:3) (see Supplemental Data).
Capillary sequencing confirmed the c.665T>C (p.Ile222>Thr) mutation (Figure 1C) and showed that it cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family.
Clinical features included moderate-to-severe ID, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphic features (Figure S1).

records.segregation: cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family
quotes: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of patient III.2 performed at the age of one year. Midline sagittal image demonstrates a very thin corpus callosum (arrows) and microcephaly (left). Axial image shows mild enlargement and asymmetry (arrowheads) of the lateral ventricles (right).

Additionally, each of the affected individuals had unique symptoms including cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairments (individual III:1), generalized seizures (III:2), and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity (II:3) (see Supplemental Data).

records.label: II:3
records.segregation: cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family
quotes: Additionally, each of the affected individuals had unique symptoms including cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairments (individual III:1), generalized seizures (III:2), and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity (II:3) (see Supplemental Data).

We ascertained a family of Morocco Jewish ancestry in the maternal line in which three male individuals were affected by an intellectual disability (ID) syndrome with apparent X-chromosomal inheritance (X-linked ID, XLID) (Figure 1A).

records.label: Two unrelated families with EIF2S3 mutations
records.segregation: Hemizygous in affected males; heterozygous in female obligate carriers
quotes: In both families, affected males presented with severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, growth retardation, and epilepsy.

A missense mutation (c.777T>G p.(Ile259Met)) and a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients, and in the heterozygous states female obligate carriers.

records.label: Index patient, family 1 (Patient 1)

phenotypes.text: non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes mellitus from 10 months
decreased muscle respiratory complex II activity
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II

records.segregation: co-segregated with disease in the family
quotes: The index patient from family 1 was born to non-consanguineous parents of Slovak origin and has one healthy older sister.

Diagnosis of MEHMO was made at the age of 10 months based on the microcephaly, partial complex epileptic seizures (diagnosed at the age of 4 months) resistant to anticonvulsives, hypogenitalism, severe mental and motor delay

Strikingly, families 1, 2 and 3 carried the identical 4 bp deletion c.1394_1397delTCAA, which co-segregated with the disease in the families and is predicted to cause a frameshift and a premature stop codon (p.Ile465Serfs*4)

records.label: Index patient, family 2 (Patient 2)

phenotypes.text: non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes mellitus from 10 months
no voluntary movements or social interaction

quotes: The index patient from family 2 is a 1st child from a Slovak non-consanguineous family with no other affected individuals known. His mother is unaffected.

MEHMO features included microcephaly, therapy resistant seizures (diagnosed at the age of 6 months) without EEG correlation, hypogenitalism, severe mental and motor delay (corresponding to 3rd month of life at the age of 2 years), central obesity
He has non-autoimmune diabetes melitus treated with insulin from 10 months.

All females from this family who carry the EIF2S3 mutation on one of their X chromosomes were unaffected.

records.label: Index patient, family 4
records.segregation: inherited from healthy mother; healthy brother not tested
quotes: MEHMO features included microcephaly, hypospadia and cryptorchidism, developmental delay, and obesity with BMI at the 97th centile (after a longer period of failure to thrive). He does not have epileptic seizures and his EEG was normal.
The patient from family 4 carried a point mutation, c.324T>A, which he inherited from his healthy mother (Figure 1A) and could not be tested in his healthy brother.
we currently interprete the p.Ser108Arg substitution as a variant of unknown significance according to American College of Medical Genetics guidelines.

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) identified the same hemizygous 4-bp deletion in the last exon of EIF2S3 (c.1394_1397delTCAA; p.Ile465Serfs*4) in affected males from 3 families with MEHMO syndrome, including the family originally reported by Steinmüller et al.; IBD analysis excluded close relationship but suggested a founder effect with distant relatedness.
quotes: Strikingly, families 1, 2 and 3 carried the identical 4 bp deletion c.1394_1397delTCAA, which co-segregated with the disease in the families and is predicted to cause a frameshift and a premature stop codon (p.Ile465Serfs*4) in the EIF2S3 encoded protein eIF2γ.
suggested a founder effect in these three families but with more distant relatedness

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) found that a yeast/human eIF2-gamma chimera carrying the Ile465Serfs*4 mutation caused slow growth exacerbated at 37 degrees C, derepressed GCN4 expression nearly 3-fold, and increased UUG/AUG initiation about 2-fold, indicating impaired eIF2 function; the yeast equivalent of Ser108Arg (Asp167Arg) had no effect.
quotes: the Ile465Serfs*4 mutation derepressed GCN4 expression nearly 3-fold, comparably to cells expressing eIF2γ-Val281Thr (Figure 4A).
the UUG/AUG ratio was increased ~2-fold in cells expressing this eIF2γ mutant compared to cells expressing the Sc/Hs chimera
yeast expressing eIF2γ-Asp167Arg as the sole source of eIF2γ exhibited no growth defects at either 30 or 37 °C, nor did the mutation affect GCN4 expression or translation start site selection

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) showed that the truncated eIF2-gamma protein was produced in patient fibroblasts, and that patient fibroblasts had 2.5-fold increased DDIT3 transcript and elevated CHOP protein, indicating activation of the integrated stress response.
quotes: These results demonstrate that eIF2γ is expressed in human fibroblasts as expected given its essential role in cellular protein synthesis, and that the C-terminal truncated protein is produced in the patients.

The DDIT3 transcript level was significantly increased (2.5-fold) in the patient relative to the controls (Figure 5A), and Western blot analysis of whole cell lysates confirmed significantly elevated CHOP protein levels

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) noted that all patients with the C-terminal frameshift mutation had the full MEHMO phenotype, whereas patients with missense mutations were less severely affected with only a subset of symptoms; they proposed that more severe EIF2S3 mutations cause full MEHMO and less deleterious ones a milder form.
quotes: All four index patients carrying the C-terminal frameshift mutation presented the full spectrum of MEHMO syndrome including microcephaly, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, hypogenitalism, and obesity. Moreover, three of the patients developed insulin-dependent diabetes in the first year of life.

In contrast, the patients with the missense mutations identified to date are less severely affected and present only subsets of symptoms that can differ even within family members carrying the same mutation.

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) found no EIF2S3 variants in the patients reported by DeLozier-Blanchet et al. and Leshinsky-Silver et al.; the latter patient carried a SERAC1 nonsense mutation, and the former family may have a mutation outside the examined region or in another gene.
quotes: While the patient reported by Leshinsky-Silver et al carried a deleterious (p.Tyr430X) mutation in the SERAC1 (MIM# 614725) gene, the genetic defect in the family reported by DeLozier-Blanchet could be located outside the EIF2S3 region examined by WES or the disease in this family might have been caused by a mutation in another gene mimicking the MEHMO syndrome.

notes.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) noted that the condition of patient 1 was markedly aggravated during intercurrent illness, with seizure exacerbation and worsened diabetes control, similar to vanishing white matter disease.
quotes: Like the VWM patients, the condition of Patient 1 in our study was markedly aggravated during periods of illness.

notes.statement: Moortgat et al. (2016) found that morpholino-based knockdown of the zebrafish EIF2S3 ortholog (eif2s3) recapitulated the human microcephaly and short stature phenotype, supporting the pathogenicity of the identified variants.
quotes: Morpholino-based knockdown of the zebrafish EIF2S3 ortholog (eif2s3) recapitulates the human microcephaly and short stature phenotype, supporting the pathogenicity of the identified variants.

notes.statement: By X-chromosome exome sequencing in 2 unrelated families with suspected X-linked syndromic intellectual disability, Moortgat et al. (2016) identified hemizygous mutations in the EIF2S3 gene, a missense (I259M) and a frameshift (Ile465SerfsTer4), in affected males; female obligate carriers were heterozygous.
quotes: X-chromosome exome sequencing was performed to identify the genetic cause of syndromic intellectual disability in two unrelated families with suspected X-linked inheritance.
Our data confirm that EIF2S3 mutation is implicated in a rare, but recognizable, form of syndromic intellectual disability.

notes.statement: In a Moroccan Jewish family with X-linked intellectual disability, Borck et al. (2012) used targeted linkage analysis to identify a 10.7-Mb candidate region on Xp22.11-p21.1 containing 35 annotated genes.
quotes: Targeted linkage analysis was performed and a candidate region spanning 10.7 megabases on the short arm of the X chromosome (Xp22.11-p21.1; Figure S2A) and containing 35 annotated genes (Figure S2B) was identified.

notes.statement: Borck et al. (2012) found the EIF2S3 c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr) variant through exome sequencing. It was absent from 188 X chromosomes from Moroccan Jewish controls, dbSNP132, the 1000 Genomes data, and more than 8,000 alleles in the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project. Ile222 lies in the GTP-binding domain and is strictly conserved in animals.
quotes: This variant was not detected in 188 X chromosomes from Morocco Jewish controls, nor was it present in dbSNP132, the 1000 Genomes data, or >8,000 alleles sequenced by the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project.
Ile222 is located in the GTP-binding (G) domain of eIF2γ (Figure 1D) and is strictly conserved in the animal kingdom

notes.statement: Borck et al. (2012) expressed tagged eIF2-gamma carrying the I222T variant in HeLa cells. Substantially less eIF2-beta was pulled down with the mutant protein, while eIF2-alpha binding was not impaired. This indicated that the mutation disrupts formation of the eIF2 complex.
quotes: Whereas eIF2α and eIF2β were co-precipitated with the tagged wild type eIF2γ on Ni2+ affinity resin (Figure 2E, lanes 3–4), substantially less eIF2β was pulled-down with eIF2γ-I222T (Figure 2E, lanes 5–6). As was observed in yeast, the I222T mutation in human eIF2γ did not impair eIF2α binding.

notes.statement: In yeast, Borck et al. (2012) studied mutations at Val281 of eIF2-gamma, the residue corresponding to human Ile222. The V281T and V281K mutations impaired eIF2-beta binding and increased GCN4-lacZ expression 2.5-fold and 40-fold, respectively. They also raised the UUG/AUG initiation ratio 2- to 3-fold, and overexpressing eIF2-beta suppressed these defects. Only V281K impaired growth.
quotes: The V281T and V281K mutations in eIF2γ increased expression of a GCN4-lacZ reporter 2.5- and 40-fold, respectively (Table 1, panel A).
The V281T and V281K mutations in eIF2γ increased the UUG/AUG initiation ratio by 2–3 fold (Table 1, panel B).

In contrast, the eIF2γ-V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2β binding (Figure 2D, lanes 5–6), indicating that a substantial loss of eIF2 integrity is tolerated in yeast without an affect on cell growth.

notes.statement: Borck et al. (2012) sequenced the EIF2S3 exons in 60 affected individuals from families with unspecific, potentially X-linked intellectual disability and found no additional mutations. The authors suggested that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype.
quotes: we did not identify additional mutations in 60 affected individuals from families with unspecific (and potentially X-linked) ID by sequencing the 12 EIF2S3 exons
suggests that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype

notes.statement: Borck et al. (2012) noted a p.V151L variant in EIF2S3 that an earlier large-scale resequencing project had reported in an XLID family. The orthologous yeast mutation, V210L, caused defects in growth, GCN4 expression, and start site selection, and these defects were suppressed by overexpressing tRNAi-Met. The authors considered a causative role plausible.
quotes: We noted that a distinct missense variant (c.451G>C, p.V151L) was previously reported by a large-scale resequencing project of X-chromosomal genes in families with XLID.

Consistently, our analysis of the orthologous V210L mutation that lies near the Met-tRNAi Met binding site in yeast eIF2γ (Figure S4A) revealed defects in cell growth, GCN4 expression and translation start site selection (Figure S4B–C).

notes.statement: Borck et al. (2012) contrasted this disorder with vanishing white matter disease, which is caused by eIF2B mutations. They noted that patients with the eIF2-gamma mutation do not show loss of white matter.
quotes: Moreover, the patients with eIF2γ mutations do not display loss of white matter; conversely, mental development is normal or only mildly delayed in early stages in most forms of VWM disease.

notes.statement: Leshinsky-Silver et al. (2002) found markedly reduced activities of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle from a child with MEHMO and lactic acidosis, with mitochondrial proliferation, lipid storage, and abnormal enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae, and concluded that MEHMO is a mitochondrial disorder, one of the very few X-linked mitochondrial syndromes.
quotes: This is the first identification of MEHMO as a mitochondrial disorder and one of the very few X-linked mitochondrial syndromes.

notes.statement: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) assigned the disease locus for MEHMO syndrome to Xp21.1-p22.13.
quotes: MEHMO, a novel syndrome: assignment of disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13.

notes.statement: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) described MEHMO as a novel syndrome characterized by mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
quotes: Mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and genitalism, microcephaly, obesity.

notes.statement: Steinmüller et al. (1998) described a previously unrecognized X-linked mental retardation syndrome characterized by mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity, which they termed MEHMO. Life expectancy of patients was less than 2 years.
quotes: A previously unrecognised X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome is described.
Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.

notes.statement: By haplotype and 2-point linkage analyses in a large 3-generation family, Steinmüller et al. (1998) assigned the MEHMO locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, in a region flanked by CYBB and DXS365.
quotes: Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, to a region that is flanked by CYBB and DXS365.

notes.statement: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) noted that their 2 brothers most resembled patients with Borjeson-Forssman-Lehmann syndrome, but that the severity of dwarfism and mental retardation was much greater than in any reported BFL patient and the neurologic and dysmorphic features differed significantly. They considered either a particularly severe, perhaps allelic, variant of BFL or a previously undescribed disorder.
quotes: Among the over 70 syndromes of X-linked mental retardation already described, our patients resemble individuals with the Börjeson-Forssman-Lehmann (BFL) syndrome the most.

However, the severity of their dwarfism and mental retardation is much greater than described in any BFL patient to date, and the neurological and dysmorphic features vary significantly from those described in the BFL.
Although a particularly severe variant, perhaps allelic, is a possibility, an as yet undescribed disorder is also plausible

notes.statement: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) considered an X-linked recessive gene tempting given the importance of the X chromosome in mental retardation, but concluded that the disorder in the 2 affected brothers would probably be recessive, either autosomal or X-linked.
quotes: it is tempting to consider an X-linked recessive gene, given the importance of the X chromosome in mental retardation.
an as yet undescribed disorder is also plausible, the etiology of which would probably be recessive, either autosomal or X-linked.
